Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.exception

Class DriverException

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Throwable
java.lang.Exception
java.lang.RuntimeException
org.aristonis.diwan.database.exception.DatabaseException
org.aristonis.diwan.database.exception.DriverException
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class DriverException extends DatabaseException
Reports a failure raised by a driver, with the database's SQL state, vendor code and kind.

The message names the SQL state and vendor code, then the recognised kinds and, on SQLite, the result code name, such as SQLITE_BUSY. It never holds bound values or the database's own error text.

Instances are immutable after construction and safe to share between threads.

See Also:
  • Serialized Form
Implementation Requirements:
A driver must build the message from a fixed description of the failure plus the SQL state and vendor code, never from bound values and never from the database's raw error text, which often echoes the offending values. The core keeps binding values out of every message it builds and shows them only when the application opts in; a message that carries them would defeat that. The raw text goes in databaseMessage() instead, which the core shows under the same opt-in. The database's own exception may be passed as the cause.

    • DriverException

      public DriverException(String message, String sqlState, int vendorCode, Throwable cause, Set<DriverFailureKind> kinds)
      Creates a driver failure.
      Parameters:
      message - the detail message, may be null
      sqlState - the SQL state the database reported, or null when it gave none
      vendorCode - the vendor-specific error code, 0 when there is none
      cause - the underlying failure, or null when there is none
      kinds - the kinds the driver assigns to this failure, never null, may be empty; the set is copied and later changes to it have no effect
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if kinds or any element of it is null

    • DriverException

      public DriverException(String message, Set<DriverFailureKind> kinds, Throwable cause)
      Creates a driver failure that carries no SQL state and no vendor code.

      Meant for failures the driver detects itself, such as a duplicate column label, where the database reported nothing. sqlState() is empty and vendorCode() is 0.

      Parameters:
      message - the detail message, may be null
      kinds - the kinds the driver assigns to this failure, never null, may be empty; the set is copied and later changes to it have no effect
      cause - the underlying failure, or null when there is none
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if kinds or any element of it is null

  • Method Details

    • databaseMessage

      public Optional<String> databaseMessage()
      Returns the database's own error text, such as no such table: users.

      The text can echo the values that caused the failure, so it is not part of Throwable.getMessage() and this field is not serialized. The cause may still hold the same text: logging or serializing the whole exception chain shows it, whatever the connection's settings.

      Returns:
      the text, or empty when the database gave none or the exception was deserialized

    • error

      public DiwanError error()
      Returns the unified error: a stable code, and the constraint name and columns when known.
      Returns:
      the error, never null; for an exception read from a stream written by an older version it is derived from the kinds and has no key and no columns
